steps.message:
All changes are in place and the project builds.

## Diagnosis

`ItemTouchHelper` translates the swiped view off screen (`translationX = ±recyclerView.getWidth()`), and the fragments additionally dim it (`onItemSelected()` → `alpha = 0.5f`). That state is only undone in `ItemTouchHelper.onChildViewDetachedFromWindow()`, which calls `Callback.clearView()` — i.e. **only when the RecyclerView actually recycles/detaches the view during a layout pass**.

When the swiped item was the *last* one, `QueueFragment.onFragmentLoaded()` did:

```java
if (queue == null || queue.size() == 0) {
    recyclerView.setVisibility(View.GONE);   // <-- the defect
    txtvEmpty.setVisibility(View.VISIBLE);
}
```

A view with visibility `GONE` is never measured or laid out by its parent, so the RecyclerView never ran the layout pass that would have detached the swiped child. `clearView()` was therefore never invoked and the view holder stayed attached, still translated fully off screen. Pressing **Undo** re-inserted the item, made the list visible again, and RecyclerView reused that very holder — exactly the reported symptom: *"Empty view is removed and list is displayed. List contains an item (layout inspector), but it seems to be moved outside of the screen."*

## Fix

**1. `QueueFragment.onFragmentLoaded()`** — stop hiding the list; only toggle the empty view, which already overlays the RecyclerView in `queue_fragment.xml` (declared after it, `match_parent`, transparent background). The RecyclerView now lays out when it becomes empty, recycles the swiped child, and `clearView()` resets the swipe state properly:

```java
txtvEmpty.setVisibility(queue == null || queue.size() == 0 ? View.VISIBLE : View.GONE);
recyclerView.setVisibility(View.VISIBLE);
```

**2. `QueueRecyclerAdapter` + `AllEpisodesRecycleAdapter`** — added a `resetSwipeState()` to each view holder (clears `alpha`, `translationX`, `translationY`) and call it at the top of `onBindViewHolder()`. This makes any (re-)bound row unconditionally visible, so a holder that retained a swipe offset can never render a restored item off screen. This covers the other affected screens, **Episodes→New** and **Episodes→Favorites**, which share `AllEpisodesRecycleAdapter`.

This is safe for in-progress gestures: `ItemTouchHelper` re-applies the translation of the selected view (and of running recover animations) on every draw frame via `Callback.onDraw()`, and drag reordering uses `notifyItemMoved()`, which repositions rather than rebinds.

extra.final_message:
All changes are in place and the project builds.

## Diagnosis

`ItemTouchHelper` translates the swiped view off screen (`translationX = ±recyclerView.getWidth()`), and the fragments additionally dim it (`onItemSelected()` → `alpha = 0.5f`). That state is only undone in `ItemTouchHelper.onChildViewDetachedFromWindow()`, which calls `Callback.clearView()` — i.e. **only when the RecyclerView actually recycles/detaches the view during a layout pass**.

When the swiped item was the *last* one, `QueueFragment.onFragmentLoaded()` did:

```java
if (queue == null || queue.size() == 0) {
    recyclerView.setVisibility(View.GONE);   // <-- the defect
    txtvEmpty.setVisibility(View.VISIBLE);
}
```

A view with visibility `GONE` is never measured or laid out by its parent, so the RecyclerView never ran the layout pass that would have detached the swiped child. `clearView()` was therefore never invoked and the view holder stayed attached, still translated fully off screen. Pressing **Undo** re-inserted the item, made the list visible again, and RecyclerView reused that very holder — exactly the reported symptom: *"Empty view is removed and list is displayed. List contains an item (layout inspector), but it seems to be moved outside of the screen."*

## Fix

**1. `QueueFragment.onFragmentLoaded()`** — stop hiding the list; only toggle the empty view, which already overlays the RecyclerView in `queue_fragment.xml` (declared after it, `match_parent`, transparent background). The RecyclerView now lays out when it becomes empty, recycles the swiped child, and `clearView()` resets the swipe state properly:

```java
txtvEmpty.setVisibility(queue == null || queue.size() == 0 ? View.VISIBLE : View.GONE);
recyclerView.setVisibility(View.VISIBLE);
```

**2. `QueueRecyclerAdapter` + `AllEpisodesRecycleAdapter`** — added a `resetSwipeState()` to each view holder (clears `alpha`, `translationX`, `translationY`) and call it at the top of `onBindViewHolder()`. This makes any (re-)bound row unconditionally visible, so a holder that retained a swipe offset can never render a restored item off screen. This covers the other affected screens, **Episodes→New** and **Episodes→Favorites**, which share `AllEpisodesRecycleAdapter`.

This is safe for in-progress gestures: `ItemTouchHelper` re-applies the translation of the selected view (and of running recover animations) on every draw frame via `Callback.onDraw()`, and drag reordering uses `notifyItemMoved()`, which repositions rather than rebinds.
